title: Feedback Request 1
description: Feedback to the makers, forwarded to the Mayor. Six forms: grammar-approach (Ask for another approach, with pictures attached), tutor-ask (an ask the tutor could not meet, sent by his tap on Send this to the makers), book (Ask for a book: one book of his Logos library, by title, with the row's Logos details when he picked it from his list), library (Ask the makers about these: the whole list of an import, once, as counts by Logos type with the usable rows attached as library.csv), the three short forms of Settings > Ask for more: approach (an approach or programme), text and translation, and tutor-misses (sent by the nightly tutor-weights run, not by him: what the tutor wanted that the app lacks, when it is worth a story).

kind.description: grammar-approach asks for another way of teaching Greek grammar.

text.description: What approach he wants and how it teaches, in his words.

name.description: Who made the approach, so the factory can credit them.

url.description: A link to the approach, when there is one.

app_version.description: The Lampas build he sent it from.

kind.description: tutor-ask is something he asked the tutor for that Lampas does not do (work with another app, a new setting, a change); the tutor offered to pass it on and he tapped Send this to the makers.

text.description: What he asked the tutor, in his words: at most 4000 characters, as long as a question to the tutor may be.

summary.description: The tutor's one-line summary of the ask.

screen.description: The screen he asked from: its name, or Reader for a talk about the text.

reference.description: What the talk was about: the screen's name, or the chapter or verse (Romans 8:28).

facts.description: What the screen showed him, as the tutor was told it. Left out when the talk was about the text.

app_version.description: The Lampas build he sent it from.

kind.description: book asks for one book of his Logos library to be added: a grammar for the idea sheets' Read more, a devotional for Which devotional, a commentary, lexicon, Greek text or interlinear, or any book he wants Lampas to open.

title.description: The book's title, and its author if he gave one, as he typed it (Mounce, Basics of Biblical Greek) or as his Logos list names it.

resource.description: Optional. The Logos Resource ID of the row he picked from his own list (LLS:46.30.18): the Mayor adds it to the rules without research. Left out when he typed the title.

type.description: Optional. The row's Logos Type (text.monograph.commentary.bible). Only with a picked row.

series.description: Optional. The row's Series, when it has one. Only with a picked row.

refs.description: Optional. The row's ReferenceSupersets cell, tokens separated by tabs (cut at a whole token when long). Only with a picked row.

kindWanted.description: Optional. The kind of book he wants, when the place he asked from names one (the idea sheet asks for a grammar, Settings > Daily for a devotional).

why.description: Optional. Why it would help him, in his words. Left out when he wrote nothing.

app_version.description: The Lampas build he sent it from.

kind.description: library is the whole list of an import, sent once when he taps Ask the makers about these. The usable rows are the attached library.csv (ResourceId, Type, Title, Series, ReferenceSupersets; text/csv, under 200 KB), never in this request.

books.description: How many books the Logos list he imported has.

usable.description: How many rows library.csv holds: the books Lampas could use and does not open yet (commentaries on the New Testament, Greek grammars and lexicons, Greek texts, interlinears, devotionals; never manuscripts).

counts.description: How many books of each Logos type Lampas cannot use yet (the app names at most the 40 types with the most books).

catalogue_version.description: The version of Lampas's catalogue of Logos books when he sent it; the next ask waits for a new one or 30 days.

app_version.description: The Lampas build he sent it from.

kind.description: An ask that would grow the app, from a short form of Settings > Ask for more: approach (an approach or programme for learning Greek), text (a text Lampas does not have: the Septuagint, another edition) or translation (an English translation to read beside the Greek).

name.description: What he wants, by name, as he typed it (The ESV, Logeion, the Polis method).

text.description: Optional. Why he wants it, or what he would use it for, in his words. Left out when he wrote nothing.

url.description: Optional. A link to it, when he gave one.

memorizing.description: Optional. His memorizing evidence, only when he turned on Include my memorizing evidence for this ask: a summary line and his recalls of the verses he memorizes (src/memorize/evidence.ts). Left out otherwise.

summary.description: One line: how many verses, recalls and passes, and the gaps between recalls (3 verses, 14 recalls, 11 passed, gaps 1 to 7 days).

evidence.description: The recalls of each verse in each language, the most recently recalled first, at most the last 30 of each, under 6,000 bytes.

ref.description: The verse as a canonical reference (Rom.8.28).

lang.description: The language he memorizes it in: en, el or weave.

rung.description: The rung asked: the schedule step, 0 (read and say) to 6 (from nothing).

score.description: The share of the words he had in order, 0 to 1.

missed.description: The words he missed, at most 12. Left out when none.

gap.description: Days since the last recall of this verse in this language, 0 for the first.

how.description: How it was heard: said, typed, mill (the verse-read grind) or self (he graded himself).

app_version.description: The Lampas build he sent it from.

kind.description: tutor-misses is sent by the nightly tutor-weights run (not by him) when it finds misses worth a story: what the tutor wanted that the app has no fact, command or place for, counted since the last run.

text.description: The misses as lines of words, one for each: the title, the screen, how often and why.

summary.description: One line: how many misses are worth a story.

title.description: What to build, as a story's title.

screen.description: The screen the tutor missed it on.

count.description: How many times it was missed since the last run.

app_version.description: The Lampas build that sent it.
